newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania trade deficit at $1.54 bln in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Romania trade deficit at $1.54 bln in 1996.

text.p: Romania's trade deficit shrank slightly to $1.54 billion last year from $1.57 billion in 1995, National Statistics Board (CNS) data showed on Friday.
"Exports were 3.2 percent down in 1996, with higher falls in metallurgy product exports, of 5.1 percent," CNS president Pavel Wagner told a news conference.
An overvalued local leu currency last year, along with a change in exports structure with stronger emphasis on foodstuffs, have triggered the negative trend in Romanian exports, a CNS report said.

The leu was kept artificially high for most of 1996 by the former leftist government, ousted in last November's polls. Its official rate fell by 56.5 percent to the dollar in 1996, when year-on-year inflation was 56.9 percent.
Last year, exports amounted to $7.66 billion, with food products topping the list, while imports stood at $9.2 billion, or 3.0 percent down on 1995.

Romania's trade balance, deteriorated over the past months due to fuel purchases to cope with a harsh winter, hit the leu, which has lost over 50 percent since January 1 to its present rate of 6,350/400 to the dollar.
The private sector accounted for 50.7 percent of 1996 exports and took 47.7 percent of Romanian imports.
Germany was Romania's leading trading partner in 1996.
NOTES -- All figures in FOB prices. The CNS 1996 import data do not include $216 million worth of oil imports whose customs documents were delayed. Data are subject to revisions.
